title: China's PPI Rebound Signals Industrial Turnaround — Why Aren't MCHI, FXI ETFs Rallying Yet?
author: Chandrima Sanyal
description: China's Producer Price Index rose 0.5% year-over-year in March 2026, marking its first expansion since September 2022. However, China-focused ETFs remain cautious as the inflation is driven by rising input costs rather than demand, raising concerns about margin sustainability. ETF investors are taking a wait-and-see approach until a demand-led recovery becomes evident.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Trading at P/E of 12.15 with no meaningful rerating despite positive PPI data. Heavy exposure to consumer discretionary and financials sectors dependent on sustained demand recovery, which remains uncertain. Investors are cautious about the quality of inflation.

Tied to long-duration earnings expectations and vulnerable if recovery fails to broaden beyond cost-driven inflation. Growth-focused positioning makes it sensitive to demand recovery uncertainty.
